checks.note: Both rules restate §8.99.010, but they are duplicates of the same single provision, so one is redundant.
The $50 cap, five-or-more-unit coverage and prohibition on landlords and agents match §8.99.010.
The §8.99.020 exemption for owner-occupied buildings with fewer than five units is captured in both rules, although it is logically redundant with the five-unit threshold.
The source is a Cambridge ordinance and the rules are assigned to Cambridge, MA.

§8.99.030 says the ordinance takes effect on the first day of the second month after enactment. The source approval date is November 20, 2026, so 2027-01-01 is a plausible reading. Even so, 'enactment' is not clearly defined, the derivation label 'nj_nth_month_next_following' is odd, and key_values carry null dates.
The quote comes from §8.99.010 and is correct. The exemption citations are null even though that text is in §8.99.020, and the effective-date section §8.99.030 is not cited.
No precedence relations are asserted, and the source contains none.
Nothing invented beyond the source. The effective-date derivation is an inference from §8.99.030.
CAM-FEE-01 and CAM-FEE-02 are duplicates of each other. The duplicates check passed, but both rules appear in the same extraction.
The coverage structure differs between the two rules, one using 'all' and one a bare predicate. Their confidence values also differ, 0.8 and 0.9, for identical content.

issues.message: CAM-FEE-02 duplicates CAM-FEE-01, and both extract the same provision.

The effective date was derived from the 'enactment' wording in §8.99.030. It was computed as 2027-01-01 with the anchor 'Approved November 20, 2026', and a human should confirm it. The date section is not cited.
The exemption citation is null, but the exemption text comes from §8.99.020.
